title: General words for thinking and communicating
blurb: Master the HESI A2 words for understanding, explaining and reasoning (infer, imply, concise, explicit, corroborate) and their look-alike traps.
question: A preceptor asks a student to give a concise report, clarify an ambiguous order and corroborate the patient's history with the family. What exactly is she being asked to do in each case?

teach.h: Words for what the mind and mouth do
teach.body: Formally, these are general academic verbs, adjectives and nouns that name mental and communication acts: understanding, judging, explaining, reasoning and agreeing. In plain English: they describe how people take in information, work things out, and pass ideas to others. Health settings use them constantly (clarify an order, a concise handoff), and HESI A2 distractors are mostly look-alikes such as collaborate/corroborate and infer/imply.

teach.caption: The person sending the hint implies; the person receiving it infers.

items: Please consult your pharmacist before taking another pain reliever (seek advice from).
The nurses collaborate on the care plan (work together).
Lab results corroborate the diagnosis (confirm it with evidence).
Bring pertinent records, such as X-rays (relevant).
Explain your rationale for the choice (the reasons behind it).
The order was ambiguous (it could be read two ways).

teach.body: Sofia Alvarez, applying to a nursing program, works as a unit clerk. The charge nurse asks for a concise handoff: brief but complete, not a long story. A handwritten order is ambiguous, so Sofia asks the provider to clarify it. The family's account of the fall corroborates the patient's own: it confirms it. When the nurse says 'I'm not sure that dose is right,' she implies doubt; Sofia infers she should double-check.

teach.text: Infer and imply are not interchangeable on the HESI A2: the listener infers, the speaker implies. And concise (brief) is not precise (exact): a short report can be imprecise, and a precise one can be long.

items: Understand and judge: comprehend, discern, analyze, evaluate, deduce, infer, validate.
Explain: clarify, elaborate, articulate; concise/succinct = brief; comprehensive = complete.
Stated vs hinted: explicit vs implicit; ambiguous = unclear, two readings.
Agree: concur, corroborate, consensus. Disagree: dispute, refute.

summary: You can now define the HESI A2 words for understanding, explaining, reasoning and agreeing, and use the speaker-implies, listener-infers rule. You can also reject look-alike traps such as collaborate for corroborate, deduct for deduce and refuse for refute.

A.q: Use plain words so that every patient can comprehend the instructions for the home test kit. What is the best definition of the word comprehend in this sentence?
A.why: Comprehend means to understand, or grasp, the meaning of something.

whyNot.3: Finishing the test is a topic fit, but comprehend means to understand the instructions.

A.q: If the rash spreads to your arms, consult your pharmacist before trying another cream. What is the best definition of the word consult in this sentence?
A.why: Consult means to seek advice or information from someone.

whyNot.2: Thanking comes after help; consult means to seek it.
whyNot.3: Paying is a topic fit at a pharmacy, but consult means to ask for advice.

A.q: After the stroke, Mr. Price struggled to articulate words clearly during his speech therapy sessions. What is the best definition of the word articulate in this sentence?
A.why: As a verb, articulate means to express or pronounce clearly.

whyNot.0: Recognizing words is understanding them; articulate is about saying them.
whyNot.1: Writing is a different skill; articulate refers to speech here.
whyNot.2: Spelling is about letters on a page; articulate means pronounce.

B.q: The doctor gave a succinct answer to the family's question about the test before rushing to the next patient. What is the best definition of the word succinct in this sentence?
B.why: Succinct means expressed clearly in few words.

whyNot.0: Wordy is the opposite of succinct.
whyNot.1: Being unsure is about certainty, not length.
whyNot.3: Distinct is a look-alike ending; succinct is about brevity.

B.q: The patient's family plans to dispute the hospital bill with their insurance company next week. What is the best definition of the word dispute in this sentence?
B.why: To dispute is to argue against or challenge something.

whyNot.0: Paying the bill is the opposite of disputing it.
whyNot.2: Reviewing comes first, but dispute means to argue against the bill.
whyNot.3: Dividing the bill is a topic fit; dispute means to challenge it.

B.q: The instructor will evaluate each student's hand-washing technique during the skills lab on Friday. What is the best definition of the word evaluate in this sentence?
B.why: Evaluate means to judge the value, quality or significance of something.

whyNot.0: Clearing out is evacuate, a look-alike.
whyNot.1: Raising up is elevate, another look-alike.
whyNot.2: Showing the technique is demonstrate; the instructor judges it.

C.q: By checking his watch again and again, the visitor seemed to imply that the doctor was running late. What is the best definition of the word imply in this sentence?
C.why: Imply means to suggest without stating directly; the visitor hints by his actions.

whyNot.0: Conclude is infer, what an observer would do; the visitor is the one sending the hint.
whyNot.2: Proving requires evidence; checking a watch only hints.
whyNot.3: Denying is the opposite of hinting that something is true.

C.q: Please list only the symptoms that are relevant to today's visit for your sore throat. What is the best definition of the word relevant in this sentence?
C.why: Relevant means closely connected to the matter at hand.

whyNot.3: Recent symptoms are a topic fit, but relevant means connected to the visit, not new.

C.q: Select the word that best completes the sentence: After reviewing the lab results, the care team reached a ____ that surgery was needed.
C.why: A consensus is a general agreement among a group; the team agreed.

whyNot.0: A census is an official count of people.
whyNot.2: A concession is something given up in a dispute.
whyNot.3: A consequence is a result; teams reach agreement, not a consequence that surgery was needed.

reteach.title: A detective's notebook
reteach.question: A detective notices clues, works out what happened, checks the story with witnesses and then explains it to the jury. How do the thinking and communicating words map onto those steps?

blocks.body: First the detective discerns a footprint (notices it) and analyzes it (examines it in detail). From the evidence she infers or deduces who was there. A witness corroborates the story; a second witness disputes it, and lab results refute his version. In court she must be concise and explicit, not ambiguous. Every step of the case has a word on the HESI A2 list.

blocks.text: The detective collaborates with her partner (works together) but corroborates the alibi (confirms it). One letter pattern, two different jobs.

explain.body: Comprehend (understand), discern (make out), analyze (examine in detail), evaluate (judge).

test.q: The lab will analyze the blood sample for signs of infection before the end of the day. What is the best definition of the word analyze in this sentence?
test.why: Analyze means to examine in detail in order to understand.

whyNot.0: Numbing is anesthetize, a look-alike in sound.
whyNot.1: Freezing is a way to store a sample, not to analyze it.
whyNot.3: Collecting the sample happens before the lab analyzes it.

explain.body: Explicit means stated plainly. Implicit means suggested but not stated. Ambiguous means it could be read more than one way.

test.q: Which word means suggested but not directly stated?
test.why: Implicit means implied or suggested without being directly stated.

whyNot.0: Explicit is the opposite: stated clearly.
whyNot.1: Illicit means forbidden by law or rules.
whyNot.2: Complicit means involved with others in wrongdoing.

explain.body: Infer and deduce both mean to reach a conclusion. Deduct means to subtract; induce means to bring about; reduce means to lessen.

test.q: Select the word that best completes the sentence: From the patient's yellowed skin and eyes, the student could ____ a liver problem.
test.why: Deduce means to reach a conclusion by reasoning from the evidence (yellowed skin).

whyNot.0: Deduct means to subtract, the look-alike.
whyNot.2: Induce means to cause; the student cannot cause the liver problem by observing it.
whyNot.3: Reduce means to lessen; observing does not lessen a liver problem.

explain.body: Collaborate means to work together. Corroborate means to support a statement with more evidence.

test.q: Select the word that best completes the sentence: Two visitors in the lobby ____ the nurse's account of how the patient fell.
test.why: Corroborate means to confirm with additional evidence; the visitors' accounts support the nurse's.

whyNot.0: Collaborate means to work together; the visitors confirmed an account, they did not work with the nurse.
whyNot.1: Elaborate means to add detail to one's own account.
whyNot.3: Calibrate means to adjust an instrument.
